chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no I'tikaf (spiritual retreat) except in the last ten days of the month of Ramadan.
And he said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: I do not consider I'tikaf to be valid except in the Sacred Mosque (Mecca), or the Prophet's Mosque (Medina), or in a congregational mosque.
And it is not fitting for the one in I'tikaf to leave the mosque except for a necessity that is unavoidable, then he should not sit [outside] until he returns.
And the woman is the same [in this ruling].
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and locations for valid I'tikaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes the preferred locations for I'tikaf, prioritizing the three holiest mosques while allowing for congregational mosques, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal worship spaces. It further clarifies the conditions for exiting the mosque, requiring the mu'takif to return immediately after fulfilling an unavoidable need, a rule applied equally to men and women, thereby highlighting the gender-neutral nature of this spiritual discipline in Shia jurisprudence.
